signature: “IOHANN ((*)) IOSEPH ((*)) SCHMIED ((*)) MACHTS ((*)) IN ((*)) PFAFFENDORFF ((*)) ANNO ((*)) 1789 ((*))((O))((*))((O))((*))”; festoon pattern.
pitch: F# slightly sharp with slide fully closed; F# with slide extended approx. 70mm.
mouthpiece: : Might be orig.; very shallow bowl, rim slightly rounded; le 105, bowl 42.3 ext., 31.3 int., depth of bowl 14.5, throat 7.2, exit 9.2 (int.)
dimensions: mp rcvr 13.8, bo1 12, bo2 12, slide sec. exit 12.4, slide sec. 2092, bell sec. 1354, overlap 41 (*est.), le 3405 (*est.), be 161, handle 345, garland 38 (surface of bell), garland 34 (axial). Measured by the author, 2/12/99
provenance: Moravian tradition suggests that the four Schmied (Schmidt) trombones in Gnadenhutten--17891, 17892, 17893, and 1804—were acquired from Lititz when that community purchased a new set.
literature: Van den Bosch 1989: 54; Heyde 1997:102; Kaufman & Hartzell 1987: 32.
remarks: Very nice sound, free-blowing; slide very stiff.Ferrules, slide stays, as in 17891; Flat bell-stay; tubular slide stays; slide handle; rings in slide- and bell-bows; handle (to permit full extension of slide) attached to moveable slide stay; moveable slide stay not telescopic; immoveable slide stay has collar (repair?) that wraps around bottom tube; saddle with sheet-metal style ring in slide bow; zigzag pattern on saddle appears to be like 17891 and 17892, but oxidation conceals part of pattern; slide bow guard as in 17892; bell stay as in 17892; collar (later repair) on bellpipe side of bell stay is loose; considerable oxidation in this location; bell bow has saddle and ring as in 17891; no guard in bell bow.
